questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go as far south in Europe as possible, to experience nicer weather and the south european culture. Academically, I found it hard to know what to expect in advance from any university, so the specific institution I applied at was not a major factor in making the decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The university was disappointing academically, as some classes were taught by professors with a limited understanding of both the English language as well as their subjects - however, some classes were really great and taught by great professors.

Everything else was great though, ie. the cultural experience

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had the good fortune of being on exchange with some fellow students from KU, and honestly I relied a lot on them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, mostly from my fellow students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I felt relatively well received by the institution, and everything was figured out eventually.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Some sites, such as Idealista, seemingly provide a sense of security against scammers. I however found my accomodation through Facebook.

Beware of scammers. I had several calls with "agents" who demanded NON-REFUNDABLE fees of thousands of euros, and I could see they were calling from Indian phone numbers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I guess the same applies here as when living in most places - investigate the area you are considering moving into. Milan felt safe, mostly, but I did occasionally experience some parts of the city where I wouldnt have felt safe living.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont know if I was exceptionally lucky, but I was satisfied with what I found, regarding price, comfort and location.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't remember it in detail, but in general everything went okay when taken one step at a time

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The whole process involved a lot of online platforms and different email accounts - this does not only apply to the host institution, but for the whole exchange process in general.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I am sure there was support available, but I mostly relied on my fellow students from KU

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100 percent

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient, take a deep breath, make a cup of coffee and sit down. Take one step at a time, read the emails carefully - and consult fellow students!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
As mentioned, some professors were really disappointing in regards to both language and academical competencies.

Others were great.

Most were inbetween. It should be mentioned that I was not particularly interested in my mandatory subjects, which might have influenced my perception.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Both levels

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In general I would say there was a lower level academically, even in master classes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Research methods, conflict management and negotiation, human resource management, inequality in the labour market

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Conflict management and negotiation - awesome class, awesome professor, who took time out of his personal schedule to take us on a guided tour of his hometown with a focus on all conflicts that had taken place there politically.

Housing DKK per month *

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Limoncello, mostly. I don't know if anything was unexpected. I spent a lot of money, and am 100 percent sure it could be done MUCH cheaper.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't take advantage of any offers, but they seemed great.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots and lots, I saw almost every type of sport listed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore the whole country as much as possible - remember you can study for exams from anywhere, so just travel and see the country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car, take a roadtrip with fellow students.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, Milan was in many ways like every other major european city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Treat them like every other human you want to socialize with; be polite, curious, openminded etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, to be honest - perhaps except the fact that Italians seem to have less spatial awareness and will just stand in the middle of supermarket aisles, taking up space

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food and restaurant culture - cheap and good.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live, laugh, love.

I mean, its hard to answer. But for me, living in the moment, laughing even when things are frustrating, and falling in love with the place or the people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just take it as it comes, and enjoy the experience - be patient with all the registration processes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural exchange with a rich culture, and the people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Establishing healthy routines, but this was important!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
